title: Deception Detection Under Biased Oversight: Can Biased Overseers Detect When Models Are Being Deceptive?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests whether oversight bias creates systematic blind spots for deception detection. This is the core mechanism of the compounding risk scenario. A positive finding (biased overseers miss targeted deception) would be a landmark result.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training a model to deceive in a bias-targeted way and comparing detection rates between biased and unbiased overseers. Conceptually clean but the deception training requires careful setup. Feasible with small models and medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two comparisons (biased vs. unbiased overseer detection rates) are needed, but the core experiment is a single setup. Training the deceptive model is the main scope risk. Could be tight at 30 hours but achievable if the deception is simple.
